title.zh: 卷五十九 司天考第二
title.raw: 卷五十九 司天考第二 Volume 59: Examination on Astronomy

sentences.zh: 昔孔子作《春秋》而天人備。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, Heaven and humanity were made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, the relation of Heaven and humanity was fully set forth.

sentences.zh: 予述本紀，書人而不書天，予何敢異於聖人哉！

translations.literal: In my Basic Annals I record people and do not record Heaven—how would I dare differ from the sage!
translations.idiomatic: In composing my Basic Annals I write of men and not of Heaven; how could I presume to depart from the sage!

translations.literal: Though the wording differs, the meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: The form of the text may differ, but the intent is the same.

sentences.zh: 自堯、舜、三代以來，莫不稱天以舉事，孔子刪《詩》、《書》不去也。

translations.literal: From Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties onward, none failed to invoke Heaven when undertaking affairs; when Confucius edited the Odes and Documents he did not remove this.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of Yao and Shun through the Three Dynasties, no one failed to cite Heaven in justifying their deeds; Confucius, in editing the Odes and Documents, left such passages intact.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖人不絕天於人，亦不以天參人。

translations.literal: For the sage does not sever Heaven from humanity, yet neither does he bring Heaven in to mingle with human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The sage neither cuts Heaven off from human life nor lets Heaven intrude into human affairs.

sentences.zh: 絕天於人則天道廢，以天參人則人事惑，故常存而不究也。

translations.literal: To sever Heaven from humanity is to abandon the Way of Heaven; to use Heaven to interfere with human affairs is to confuse what people must do—therefore he keeps both present without probing to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Cut Heaven off from men and the heavenly order is abandoned; let Heaven meddle in human affairs and public life falls into confusion—hence he holds both in view without pressing each to its ultimate ground.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》雖書日食、星變之類，孔子未嘗道其所以然者，故其弟子之徒，莫得有所述於後世也。

translations.literal: Though the Spring and Autumn records such things as eclipses and stellar irregularities, Confucius never spoke of their causes; thus his disciples had nothing to pass down to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn does note solar eclipses, shifting stars, and the like, yet Confucius never explained why they occurred; his disciples therefore had nothing on this subject to transmit to posterity.

translations.literal: Then does Heaven in fact participate in human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Does Heaven, then, truly take part in human affairs?

translations.literal: Or does it in fact not participate?
translations.idiomatic: Or does it truly not?

sentences.zh: 曰：天，吾不知，質諸聖人之言可也。

translations.literal: One says: As for Heaven, I do not know; let us test the question against the words of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: The answer must be: of Heaven I cannot speak with certainty; we may settle the question only by appeal to what the sage said.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天道虧盈而益謙，地道變盈而流謙，鬼神害盈而福謙，人道惡盈而好謙。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The Way of Heaven diminishes what is full and augments what is humble; the Way of Earth transforms what is full and pours forth toward what is humble; spirits and ghosts harm what is full and bless what is humble; the way of humanity detests what is full and loves what is humble."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes states: "The way of Heaven diminishes the full and augments the modest; the way of Earth transforms abundance and channels it toward modesty; spirits harm the proud and favor the humble; the way of man loathes excess and delights in modesty."

sentences.zh: 」此聖人極論天人之際，最詳而明者也。

translations.literal: This is where the sage discusses the border of Heaven and humanity most exhaustively and clearly.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sage's fullest and clearest statement on the relation between Heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 其於天地鬼神，以不可知為言，其可知者人而已。

translations.literal: Concerning Heaven, Earth, and the spirits, he speaks of what cannot be known; what can be known is humanity alone.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Heaven, Earth, and the spirits he speaks only of what cannot be known; what can be known is man alone.

translations.literal: When the sun reaches midday it declines; fullness and decline necessarily alternate.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun stands at noon it must decline; abundance and decay inevitably reverse.

sentences.zh: 天，吾不知，吾見其虧益於物者矣。

translations.literal: Heaven—I do not know it; but I see how it diminishes and augments things.
translations.idiomatic: Of Heaven I cannot speak with knowledge; yet I see how it diminishes and augments things.

sentences.zh: 草木之成者，變而衰落之；

translations.literal: What among plants and trees has grown to fullness changes and is made to decline;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever among trees and grasses has reached maturity is transformed and brought low;

translations.literal: what lies beneath is advanced and given flow.
translations.idiomatic: whatever lies low is advanced and set flowing.

sentences.zh: 地，吾不知，吾見其變流於物者矣。

translations.literal: Earth—I do not know it; but I see how it transforms and pours forth upon things.
translations.idiomatic: Of Earth I cannot speak with knowledge; yet I see how it transforms things and sets them flowing.

sentences.zh: 人之貪滿者多禍，其守約者多福。

translations.literal: Among men, those greedy for fullness mostly meet calamity; those who keep to restraint mostly receive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Men who grasp after excess mostly suffer misfortune; those who hold to restraint mostly enjoy good fortune.

sentences.zh: 鬼神，吾不知，吾見人之禍福者矣。

translations.literal: Spirits and ghosts—I do not know them; but I see men's calamities and blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Of spirits and ghosts I cannot speak with knowledge; yet I see how fortune and misfortune visit men.

sentences.zh: 天地鬼神，不可知其心，則因其著於物者以測之。

translations.literal: Heaven, Earth, and the spirits—their minds cannot be known; one can only measure them by what manifests in things.
translations.idiomatic: The minds of Heaven, Earth, and the spirits cannot be known; we may infer them only from what appears in the things they affect.

sentences.zh: 故據其跡之可見者以為言，曰虧益，曰變流，曰害福。

translations.literal: Therefore, relying on traces that can be seen, one speaks of diminishing and augmenting, of transforming and flowing, of harming and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence, judging by visible traces, one speaks of diminishment and increase, of transformation and flow, of harm and blessing.

sentences.zh: 若人則可知者，故直言其情曰好惡。

translations.literal: As for humanity, which can be known, one states its disposition directly and calls it love and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: With man, who can be known directly, one may state his feelings plainly as likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 其知與不知，異辭也，參而會之，與人無以異也。

translations.literal: To speak of what is known and what is unknown is to use different words; yet bring them together and compare, and there is no difference from humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the language speaks of what can or cannot be known differs; yet compare the two, and Heaven is not ultimately unlike man.

sentences.zh: 其果與於人乎，不與於人乎，則所不知也。

translations.literal: Whether Heaven truly participates in human affairs or does not—this is what cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Whether it truly participates in human affairs or does not remains unknowable.

sentences.zh: 以其不可知，故常尊而遠之；

translations.literal: Because it cannot be known, one habitually honors it and keeps it at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: Because it cannot be known, we honor it and hold it at a distance;

sentences.zh: 以其與人無所異也，則修吾人事而已。

translations.literal: because in respect to humanity it is not different, one need only cultivate human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: because in the end it is not different from man, we need only attend to human affairs.

translations.literal: Human affairs are the will of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Human affairs are the will of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「天視自我民視，天聽自我民聽。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Heaven sees as my people see; Heaven hears as my people hear."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "Heaven sees as my people see; Heaven hears as my people hear."

sentences.zh: 」未有人心悅於下而天意怒於上者，未有人理逆於下而天道順於上者。

translations.literal: Never has the people's hearts below been pleased while Heaven's will above was angry; never has human order below been perverse while the heavenly way above was compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Never were the hearts of the people pleased below while Heaven's will was wrathful above; never was human order overturned below while the heavenly way ran smooth above.

sentences.zh: 然則王者君天下，子生民，布德行政，以順人心，是之謂奉天。

translations.literal: Thus when a king rules all under Heaven, treats the people as children, spreads virtue and conducts government to accord with the people's hearts—this is called serving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When a true king rules the realm, nurtures the people as his children, spreads virtue and governs in accord with the people's hearts, this is what it means to serve Heaven.

sentences.zh: 至於三辰五星常動而不息，不能無盈縮差忒之變，而占之有中有不中，不可以為常者，有司之事也。

translations.literal: As for the sun, moon, stars, and five planets, they constantly move without rest and cannot be free of variations and slight deviations; that divination sometimes hits and sometimes misses and cannot be treated as constant is the business of the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, moon, stars, and five planets move ceaselessly and cannot be without irregularities of excess and deficiency; that prognostication sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails and cannot be held as fixed law is the concern of the official astronomers.

sentences.zh: 本紀所述人君行事詳矣，其興亡治亂可以見。

translations.literal: The Basic Annals describe rulers' conduct in detail; their rise and fall, order and disorder, can be discerned from them.
translations.idiomatic: The Basic Annals record rulers' deeds at length, from which their rise and fall and the fortunes of order and chaos may be read.

sentences.zh: 至於三辰五星逆順變見，有司之所占者，故以其官誌之，以備司天之所考。

translations.literal: As for the advancing, retreating, and transformations of the three luminaries and five planets—these the relevant offices observe—therefore I record them in the office devoted to them, to supply material for the Examination on Heaven's Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The irregular motions and appearances of the three luminaries and five planets are what the observing offices track; I therefore record them under that office, for the Examination on Astronomy to use.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，聖人既沒，而異端起。

translations.literal: Alas! After the sage perished, heterodox doctrines arose.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—once the sage was gone, strange doctrines sprang up.

sentences.zh: 自秦、漢以來，學者惑於災異矣，天文五行之說，不勝其繁也。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward scholars have been bewildered by portents and anomalies; theories of astronomy and the Five Phases have grown beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han, scholars have been lost in omens and prodigies; doctrines of astronomy and the Five Phases have multiplied beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 予之所述，不得不異乎《春秋》也，考者可以知焉。

translations.literal: What I relate cannot but differ from the Spring and Autumn; those who examine may understand why.
translations.idiomatic: What I record here could not but differ from the Spring and Autumn—those who study the matter will see why.

translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jiazi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年二月丁巳，歲犯咸池。

translations.literal: Guangshun, year 1, second month, day dingsi: Jupiter encroached upon Salty Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangshun, second month, on dingsi day, Jupiter encroached upon Salty Pool.

translations.literal: Day jiwei: Mars encroached upon the Five Feudal Lords.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Mars encroached upon the Five Feudal Lords.

translations.literal: Third month, day jiazi: Jupiter guarded Heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiazi day, Jupiter stood at Heart.

translations.literal: Day jimao: Mars encroached upon Ghost;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Mars encroached upon Ghost;

translations.literal: Day renwu: Mars encroached upon the Heavenly Corpse.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Mars encroached upon the Heavenly Corpse.

translations.literal: Fourth month, day jiawu: Jupiter encroached upon the Curved Halberds.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jiawu day, Jupiter encroached upon the Curved Halberds.

sentences.zh: 二年二月庚寅，太白經天。

translations.literal: Year 2, second month, day gengyin: Venus crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, second month, on gengyin day, Venus crossed the meridian in daylight.

translations.literal: Fourth month, new moon of bingxu: the sun suffered an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on the bingxu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

translations.literal: Seventh month, day yichou: Mars encroached upon the Well Halberd;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on yichou day, Mars encroached upon the Well Halberd;

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yiwei: Mars encroached upon the Heavenly Kettle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiwei day, Mars encroached upon the Heavenly Kettle.

translations.literal: Ninth month, day xinyou: Mars encroached upon Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinyou day, Mars encroached upon Ghost.

translations.literal: Day gengchen: Venus occulted the Right Law-Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Venus occulted the Right Law-Enforcer.

translations.literal: Tenth month, day renchen: Venus encroached upon Promoting the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on renchen day, Venus encroached upon Promoting the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 三年四月乙丑，熒惑犯靈臺；

translations.literal: Year 3, fourth month, day yichou: Mars encroached upon the Spiritual Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, fourth month, on yichou day, Mars encroached upon the Spiritual Terrace;

translations.literal: Fifth month, day xinsi: Mars encroached upon the Supreme General;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinsi day, Mars encroached upon the Supreme General;

translations.literal: Day bingshen: Mars encroached upon the Right Law-Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Mars encroached upon the Right Law-Enforcer.

translations.literal: Seventh month, day yiyou: the moon transgressed Room.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on yiyou day, the moon transgressed Room.

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day wushen: glaze ice rained on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wushen day, glaze ice coated the trees.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年正月庚寅，有大星墜，有聲如雷，牛馬皆逸，京城以為曉鼓，皆伐鼓以應之。

translations.literal: Xiande, year 1, first month, day gengyin: a great star fell; there was a sound like thunder; oxen and horses all fled; the capital thought it was the dawn drum, and all beat drums in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande, first month, on gengyin day a great meteor fell with a thunderous roar; cattle and horses stampeded; the capital mistook it for the dawn drum and everyone beat drums in reply.

sentences.zh: 三年正月壬戌，有星孛於參。

translations.literal: Year 3, first month, day renxu: a broom star appeared at Triaster.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, first month, on renxu day a comet appeared at Triaster.

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day gengwu: a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengwu day, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

translations.literal: Day guiyou: the moon suffered an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五代亂世，文字不完，而史官所記亦有詳略，其日、月、五星之變，大者如此。

translations.literal: In the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties the written record is incomplete, and what the historiographers noted is itself sometimes detailed and sometimes sparse; the major changes of the sun, moon, and five planets are as set forth above.
translations.idiomatic: In the turbulent age of the Five Dynasties the written record is incomplete, and what the court historians recorded is itself uneven in detail; the principal phenomena of the sun, moon, and five planets are as set forth above.

sentences.zh: 至於氣祲之象，出沒銷散不常，尤難占據。

translations.literal: As for manifestations of vapors and omens, their appearing, vanishing, dispersing, and dissolving are irregular and especially hard to fix for prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: As for signs of vapors and atmospheric portents, their rising, fading, and dispersal are irregular and especially difficult to interpret.

sentences.zh: 而五代之際，日有冠珥、環暈、纓紐、負抱、戴履、背氣，十日之中常七八，其繁不可以勝書，而背氣尤多。

translations.literal: Yet in the age of the Five Dynasties the sun often showed coronas, ear-rings, ring halos, tassel knots, bearing and embracing, wearing and treading, and back-breath—seven or eight days in ten—and the abundance cannot all be written down; back-breath was especially frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Five Dynasties the sun often bore coronas, pendant rays, ring halos, knotted streamers, and the forms of bearing, embracing, wearing, and treading upon it, with back-glory especially common—seven or eight days in ten—and the profusion cannot all be recorded.

sentences.zh: 天福八年正月丙戌，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: Tianfu, year 8, first month, day bingxu: yellow mist blocked all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianfu, first month, on bingxu day, yellow mist closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 九年正月乙未，大霧中二白虹相偶。

translations.literal: Year 9, first month, day yiwei: amid great fog two white rainbows paired with each other.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, first month, on yiwei day, amid heavy fog two white rainbows appeared paired together.

sentences.zh: 四月庚戌，大霧中有蒼白二虹。

translations.literal: Fourth month, day gengxu: amid great fog there were blue-white and white rainbows.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on gengxu day, amid heavy fog there appeared a blue-white and a white rainbow.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年十一月甲子，白虹竟天。

translations.literal: Guangshun, year 1, eleventh month, day jiazi: a white rainbow spanned the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangshun, eleventh month, on jiazi day, a white rainbow stretched across the sky.

translations.literal: These were the most extraordinary of them.
translations.idiomatic: These were among the most extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 至於吳火出楊林江水中、閩天雨豆之類，皆非中國耳目所及者，不可得而悉書矣。

translations.literal: As for such things as fire appearing in the Yanglin River in Wu, or beans raining from the sky in Min—these were not within the sight or hearing of the Central States and cannot all be fully written down.
translations.idiomatic: As for such things as fire rising from the Yanglin River in Wu or beans raining from the sky in Min—events beyond what the Central States could witness—they cannot all be recorded in full.
